Do you thrive in the sweet spot between international B2B sales, strategic business development and complex negotiations - in a role with real commercial impact? Join Danpo to drive Scandi Standard’s international QSR business by winning new customers, developing strategic partnerships and turning market opportunities into profitable growth.

Drive international growth through new QSR partnerships

Danpo is part of Scandi Standard, one of Europe’s leading poultry producers, with more than 4,000 employees and well-known brands across Northern Europe. Serving more than one billion meals annually, the Group focuses on growth through innovation, operational excellence and strong customer partnerships, with Ready-to-Eat (RTE) products and international QSR customers as key priorities.

To support this ambition, Danpo is looking for an International Key Account Manager QSR to expand the Group’s international customer base and turn market opportunities into profitable business. You will join the European Markets & QSR team, working across Sales, Category, Development and Business Development to develop customer solutions that profitable growth. Guided by Scandi Standard’s vision, “Better chicken for a better life”, you will help build partnerships that create value for both customers and the business.

Your key responsibilities include:

• Actively prospect and win new international QSR customers, taking opportunities from first contact to signed agreement and launch.

• Map the QSR market, identify priority targets and build a focused prospect list across relevant countries and customer segments.

• Create access to key decision-makers through proactive outreach, networking, referrals and persistent follow-up.

• Develop and execute clear go-to-market and customer acquisition plans for the international QSR channel.

• Build and actively manage a strong, qualified opportunity pipeline with clear next steps, conversion milestones and commercial priorities.

• Lead new-business pitches, customer tenders, contract negotiations and the commercial onboarding of new accounts.

• Drive profitable growth from both new wins and selected existing accounts, with clear ownership of customer P&L and budget performance.

• Work closely with NPD, Quality, Supply Chain, Production, Finance and Customer Service to create competitive customer solutions.

• Translate customer and market needs into product, assortment and innovation opportunities.

• Monitor customer developments, market movements and competitor activity, and convert insight into action.

• Use relevant sales tools, KPIs and performance management disciplines to create transparency and momentum.

The position can be based at a Scandi Standard office in Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland, Ireland, the Netherlands or Lithuania. You will report to Rasmus Vinther, Sales & Category Director RTE & QSR. The role involves international travel of approximately 40–50%, depending on business needs.

On behalf of KINRADEN, MINDWEISS is seeking a commercially minded and hands-on Finance Director to play a key role in the company’s next phase of international growth. With responsibility for strengthening financial management and developing a scalable finance function, you will have significant influence on strategic decisions and the financial foundation supporting KINRADEN’s ambitious retail expansion.

As Finance Director, you will report directly to the CEO and work closely with the wider management team, acting as a trusted financial and strategic sparring partner. You will take full ownership of the finance function, balancing strategic priorities with operational responsibilities while ensuring that financial insights actively support commercial decisions and future investments.

A central part of your responsibility will be to drive financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and performance management, ensuring reliable financial oversight and clear insights into business performance across the organisation and its growing retail operations. You will support strategic and commercial decision-making through financial analysis, business cases and scenario planning, including evaluating the financial implications of new stores, markets and investments.

Furthermore, you will be responsible for cash flow and liquidity management, financial controls and the preparation of relevant management and Board reporting, ensuring transparency and a clear overview of the company’s financial position.

You will also oversee the ongoing financial operations, including monthly closing, annual accounts, audits, tax, VAT and financial compliance. As KINRADEN continues to expand internationally, you will play a key role in developing scalable financial processes, systems and governance to support increasing business complexity and long-term growth.

Strong financial expertise and commercial understanding

To succeed in this role, you bring solid experience from a senior finance position and strong expertise in financial accounting, controlling, budgeting, forecasting and cash flow management. Your ability to combine financial expertise with commercial understanding enables you to support strategic decisions and evaluate business opportunities.

We expect you to have a relevant academic degree in finance, accounting or economics, ideally complemented by experience from an international business with multiple legal entities. A background in retail, consumer goods or luxury would be an advantage, although specific industry experience is not essential. Furthermore, you are fluent in English, have excellent Microsoft Office skills and are able to communicate financial insights clearly and effectively.

A grounded and collaborative finance leader

On a personal level, you are grounded, confident and approachable, with the professional maturity to build trust through your expertise and sound judgement. You take ownership naturally and work independently, while maintaining a collaborative and down-to-earth approach. To thrive in this role, it is essential that you are comfortable navigating changing priorities and can move seamlessly between strategic discussions and hands-on execution. Furthermore, your flexibility and pragmatic mindset enable you to contribute positively to KINRADEN’s informal and creative culture.

About KINRADEN

Founded in 2014 by Sarah Emilie Müllertz, KINRADEN is a modern luxury brand shaped by influences ranging from Japanese design traditions to Danish architecture. With a deep commitment to sustainability, the brand actively supports two of the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals: ensuring fair and dignified employment practices (Goal 8), and advocating for responsible production and consumption (Goal 12).

KINRADEN operates with a flat organizational structure and a work culture built on trust, responsibility, and a welcoming, down-to-earth atmosphere. The company embraces a distinctly Danish way of working—informal, friendly, and rooted in strong relationships. Collaboration is key, fostering a close-knit community where people support one another and value inclusivity.

Apply for the Position

Does this sound like the right opportunity for you? We would very much like to hear from you. Please apply by clicking the “Apply” button in this job posting and uploading your CV. Interviews will be held on an ongoing basis, and the position will be closed once the right candidate has been found.

We place emphasis on your competencies, qualifications, and ambitions, as well as a strong mutual fit between you and the company’s culture and values. Therefore, we encourage you not to include age, photo, nationality, or marital status in your CV. The right match is always about more than an impressive CV.

**Senior Data Analyst – SAP Reporting & Stakeholder Alignment

**

• Location: Copenhagen, Denmark or Lisbon, Portugal

• Working hours: Full-time

• Work model: Hybrid

• Contract type: Permanent

Are you passionate about turning business questions into meaningful data solutions? Do you enjoy working with stakeholders, solving complex data challenges, and transforming data into insights that drive better decisions? Then you might be the person we are looking for.

As our new Senior Data Analyst, you will join the Data & Insights team and report directly to the Head of Data & Insights. In this role, you will act as the bridge between business stakeholders and SAP data, ensuring reporting requirements are clearly defined, translated into actionable data solutions, and delivered with accuracy and impact.

You will work closely with Finance, Sales, Supply Chain, Operations, and Data Engineering teams to support data-driven decision-making while improving reporting processes and data quality across the organization. This is a great opportunity to influence business decisions, collaborate across functions, and help shape the future of data and analytics at STG.

**What Your Day Will Look Like

**In this role, you will typically focus on:

• Partner directly with business stakeholders — Finance leadership, Sales/Commercial, Supply Chain/Operations — to understand their reporting and data needs, and translate them into concrete data requirements.

• Work closely with data engineers to scope, request, and validate data pulled from SAP, acting as the translation layer between business language and technical/data specifications.

• Write and optimize SQL queries to extract, validate, and consolidate data for recurring and ad hoc reporting.

• Build and maintain Excel-based models, trackers, and reports that stakeholders rely on for decision-making.

• Consolidate data into stakeholder-ready reporting, and supporting data checks.

• Act as the go-to person for scoping ambiguous stakeholder requests — clarifying what's actually needed, managing expectations, and pushing back constructively when a request isn't well-defined or feasible.

• Identify data quality issues at the source and work with SAP module owners and data engineers to resolve them.

• Document data definitions, sources, and logic so reporting stays consistent and auditable month over month.

• Continuously look for ways to streamline the process rather than repeating manual work each cycle.

**What You'll Bring

**

• 5+ years of experience in a data analyst, business analyst, or similar data-facing role, ideally in a retail or consumer business.

• Strong SQL skills — comfortable writing and troubleshooting complex queries independently.

• Advanced Excel skills (pivot tables, lookups, data modeling; Power Query is a plus).

• Familiarity with SAP data structures, particularly FI (Finance) and SD (Sales & Distribution).

• Experience with SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), or willingness to learn it, is a plus.

• Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field (Business, Economics, Finance, Data/Statistics, Engineering, or related).

• Proven experience gathering requirements from business stakeholders and translating them into technical/data specifications.

• Strong stakeholder management skills — able to align multiple stakeholders (including Finance, Sales, Supply Chain, and IT/data engineering) with sometimes competing priorities, and communicate trade-offs clearly.

• Comfortable operating with a degree of ambiguity and turning it into a structured plan.

**Working At STG & What To Expect

**At Scandinavian Tobacco Group (STG), we are so much more than what meets the eye. We combine the strength of global brands with the entrepreneurial mindset that allows people to make a real impact. Here you'll have the opportunity to grow your career, collaborate across borders, and help shape what's next.

At STG you'll find more than a role. You'll find opportunities to grow, learn from talented colleagues, and contribute to initiatives that help drive business performance across a global organization.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area, and relevant market benchmarks.

**Ready to be part of something bigger?

**Apply now and discover much more.

**Our recruitment process

****Requirements

**Before starting our hiring process, your application will be reviewed by a member of our Talent Acquisition team. We assess each application against the key competencies and requirements for the role. If your experience and skills are a good match, you'll be invited to continue through our hiring process, which may include the following steps:

• Recruiter screen

• Interview with the hiring team

• Final interview with key stakeholders

Scandinavian Tobacco Group is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Are you an experienced SEO specialist with strong technical, content and analytical skills, and a curiosity for how AI is reshaping search?

We are looking for a Senior SEO Manager to join the Organic Discovery team at Transact, part of Omnicom Media. You will work across technical SEO, content strategy, performance analysis and Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO), helping clients navigate a rapidly evolving search landscape.

Working closely with the SEO Director and wider team, you will contribute to client strategy while remaining hands-on with delivery. This is a varied agency role that requires strong prioritisation skills, commercial thinking and the ability to deliver high-quality work across multiple clients and projects.

**Your role

**As Senior SEO Manager, you will develop and support Organic Discovery strategies that drive visibility, traffic and business results.

You will work across technical SEO, content strategy and performance analysis, translating data and insights into clear recommendations and action plans. You will also help clients understand how AI-driven search and Large Language Models are changing discovery and content requirements.

The role combines strategic thinking with practical execution and offers the opportunity to shape how we approach GEO and emerging search behaviours.

**Key responsibilities

**

• Develop SEO and Organic Discovery strategies across technical SEO, content and AI-driven search.

• Create content strategies and roadmaps based on audience needs, search demand, competitive analysis and business objectives.

• Deliver technical SEO audits and recommendations covering areas such as crawling, indexation, site architecture, internal linking and structured data.

• Analyse performance data using tools such as GA4, Google Search Console, Ahrefs, Semrush and Screaming Frog to identify opportunities and diagnose performance changes.

• Support the development of GEO and AI search capabilities through research, testing and experimentation.

• Create compelling, client-facing presentations that translate complex analysis into clear recommendations.

• Participate in client meetings, workshops and presentations as a trusted SEO advisor.

• Collaborate with specialists across paid search, social, analytics and media.

• Support colleagues through knowledge sharing, feedback and mentoring.

**Who are you?

**We imagine you:

• Have 4-5+ years of hands-on SEO experience, ideally in an agency or multi-client environment.

• Have strong technical SEO, content strategy and analytical skills.

• Can turn complex data into clear insights, recommendations and business impact.

• Have experience developing content strategies based on audience behaviour, search demand and performance data.

• Are familiar with GEO, AI search and Large Language Models, and eager to deepen your expertise.

• Are highly proficient in Excel and comfortable working with large datasets.

• Have strong PowerPoint and presentation skills.

• Can confidently communicate with clients and stakeholders of varying technical knowledge.

• Thrive in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities.

• Enjoy collaborating, sharing knowledge and supporting others.

• Fluency in English is essential, while knowledge of one or more Nordic languages is a welcome bonus.

You do not need to know everything about GEO and AI search. What matters is a strong SEO foundation, excellent analytical and content capabilities, sound judgement and a willingness to keep learning.

As this is a highly collaborative role, we are looking for someone who enjoys being part of an in-person team environment and can be present in our Copenhagen office multiple days per week. Please note that relocation assistance is not available for this position, and applicants should have the legal right to live and work in Denmark.

**What we offer

**At Omnicom Media, you will join one of the largest Organic Discovery teams in the region and work with national and international clients across a wide range of industries.

You will collaborate with specialists across media, data, technology, content and marketing, while benefiting from access to Omnicom's global network of more than 4,000 specialists.

**Interested?

**If you are an experienced SEO specialist looking for your next step and excited about the future of search and AI-driven discovery, we would love to hear from you. What matters most is that you bring strong SEO expertise, strategic thinking, curiosity, collaboration and the drive to keep developing your craft. If you have any questions about the role, please feel free to contact our SEO Director, Rebecca Booth (rebecca.booth@omc.com).

To ensure a fair and consistent recruitment process, all applications must be submitted through the official application channel. Direct applications via email or LinkedIn will not be considered.

Who We Are

For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become the world's leading provider of integrated investment management solutions. We are 3,500+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds in general.

SimCorp is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a culture where diverse perspectives and expertise are integrated in our everyday work. We believe in the continual growth and development of our employees, so that we can provide best-in-class solutions to our clients.

While striving to deliver client value, we believe it is vital to consider our people and our planet in every business decision we make. Acting responsibly is not optional. It is essential.

Why This Role is Important to Us

We are looking for Software Engineers at middle level to join our engineering team that builds fintech solutions for managing OTC (Over-The-Counter) financial instruments within our asset management platform, SimCorp Dimension and SimCorp One. Our work delivers value in two major areas. First, we implement new features that drive the business forward and shape the future of our platform. Second, we focus on extending and maintaining our established solutions to ensure our clients’ operations remain uninterrupted and always available.

What You Will Be Responsible For

• 
Designing, building, and extending existing solutions and APIs for our OTC asset management product, delivering value to customers incrementally.

• 
Working primarily in C#. Our codebase also includes OCaml and APL therefore prior experience with these languages is a strong plus.

• 
Understanding, refactoring and modernizing our legacy codebase without disrupting the business it supports.

• 
Focusing on the systems as a whole and being able address fundamental changes that improves the quality, performance and user experience.

• 
Collaborating closely with your product owner to refine requirements, clarify business needs, and shape how features get built.

• 
Working as part of a team of skilled engineers — pairing, reviewing code, and sharing ownership of the solution with fellow engineers.

• 
Following good engineering practice: clean code, automated testing, and CI/CD.

• 
Building, extending and consuming REST APIs.

• 
Communicating clearly with both technical and business stakeholders.

• 
Continuously learning — and helping the team and product grow with you.

Required Skills & Experience

• Interest in creating innovative features for a complex platform, working on areas such as API scalability, automation, performance, and operational resilience - having space to explore, design and influence the final solution.

• Good C# skills. This is the core language for the role; your level of seniority will determine how much ownership and architectural input you're expected to bring.

• Experience with, or genuine interest in, functional programming. Familiarity with OCaml, APL, F#, Standard ML, Scala or Haskell is a real advantage but not required — a willingness to learn is what matters most.

• Experience (or strong interest) in refactoring existing code and working with legacy systems.

• Good collaboration and communication skills, with fluency in English (written and spoken).

• A relevant degree (Computer Science or STEM) with demonstrated hands-on experience in software engineering.

Furthermore, We Value That You Are:

• motivated to work within the financial domain,

• comfortable working closely with a cross-functional team,

• willing to learn and pick up new languages and paradigms as needed,

• able to identify tech debt and help drive incremental improvement,

• a collaborative person willing to share knowledge and learn from your team members.

Our Team and Ways of Working

We deliver solution for large scale financial institutions with billions of dollars in managed assets. Therefore, our work impacts everyday of our customers operations. You will work in a small team of highly skilled engineers on whole SDLC process – from understanding customers' needs, through solutioning and design to coding, testing and maintaining our software. Our hybrid model of working includes two days (minimum) in our Copenhagen office and up to three days working remotely. Codebase includes a mix of C#, OCaml and APL which gives broad opportunities to upskill and drive your career with us. We invest a lot in your understanding of both the technical details of the solution and financial knowledge that will allow you to contribute to building the future of asset management.

Our Benefits

Competitive salary, bonus scheme, and pension are essential for any work agreement. However, at SimCorp, we believe we can offer more. Therefore, in addition to the traditional benefit scheme, we provide an excellent work-life balance: flexible work hours, a hybrid workplace model. On top of that, we have IP innovation sprints, where you have dedicated time per quarter to spend on mastering your skills as well as contributing to the company development. There is never just one route — we practice an individual approach to professional development to support the direction you want to take.

Next Steps

Please click below to apply. Applications are continuously assessed, so please send your CV in English as soon as possible. If you are interested in being a part of SimCorp but are not sure this role is the right fit, submit your CV anyway. SimCorp is on an exciting growth journey, and our Talent Acquisition Team is ready to help you discover the right role for you. The approximate time to consider your CV is three weeks. We are eager to continually improve our talent acquisition process and make everyone's experience positive and valuable. Therefore, during the process, we will ask you to provide your feedback, which is highly appreciated.

Every year, European governments spend billions on mobility: subsidies, contracts, licences, public transport. Most of that money is spent with no clear idea of what it buys for society.

We're building the tech layer that changes that.

What we do

Impact Market builds MIMA, the Mobility Impact Market. On our platform, cities and transport authorities incentivise mobility operators (bike share, e-scooters, car-pooling, car sharing, bike leasing) for trips according to their benefit to society: a car trip replaced, emissions avoided, space and congestion saved, health improved, a neighbourhood connected. By estimating the socio-economic impact of each trip, we design smart incentives that get the most social value out of public funds.

The idea is much bigger than mobility: governments paying for the outcomes they want, with the evidence to back it up. Mobility is our first market, and we intend to move into other areas of public spending.

Where we are

• 
Funded with 12+ months runway

• 
Several paying public-sector clients

• 
A production platform (prod + staging), with live trip and rider-survey data from operators flowing in since August 2026

• 
A team of 3. You'd be number 4.

The role

You'll be our first technical hire and will lead product and engineering. For now that means hands fully dirty: you write the code. No agencies, no outsourcing.

• 
Own the platform. Rust, Postgres, cloud, our RiderSurvey API, and the data pipelines from operators. You'll inherit a working MVP and decide what to keep, what to rebuild and what to build next.

• 
Make the big calls, including the language. We chose Rust deliberately: we think a strict compiler and type system are the right guardrails for building fast with AI. If you have a better argument for something else, convince us.

• 
Be AI-native. We expect you to use AI seriously in coding and every other technical task. That's how a team of four does the work of fifteen.

• 
Build agents that run the company with us, for account management, client reporting and forecasting.

• 
Grow into the science. Together with a future R&D lead, you'll work on the statistical significance of measured impacts and on forecasting how markets respond to incentives.

• 
Shape the product with the founders and our clients. You'll be in the room with transport authorities, not behind a ticket queue.

You

• 
Have minimum 4 years of relevant experience shipping production software, ideally backend or data-heavy systems

• 
Senior and still love writing code every day? Even better.

• 
Know Rust, or are genuinely motivated to go deep in it (not just "willing"). (We are not dogmatic about Rust, but we have a working platform built with care, so changing direction would take strong conviction.)

• 
Already build with AI tools daily and have opinions about how to do it well

• 
Are comfortable with data: SQL, pipelines, and an appetite for statistics and forecasting

• 
Take ownership when things are ambiguous, and like it when nobody tells you how

• 
Care about the mission. You don't need to have read our founder's book, The Next Democracy, but its core ideas about how citizens and governments could work together - is fundamental to what we do. If they don’t excite you, this probably isn't the right fit.

Bonus points for experience in mobility or transport, govtech, causal inference or experimentation, or privacy-by-design and GDPR.

A real say in everything. Stack, product, architecture, culture and who we hire next.

About Photoncycle

Solar panels make plenty of power in summer and very little in winter, when we need it most. Photoncycle solves that for households. We store energy from the summer sun, so that the it can be used all winter. When there’s excess energy, we sell the surplus to the grid, where it helps balance supply and demand. Households pay a fixed monthly fee; we build, install and operate the system.

Our mission is to accelerate the transition to a more renewable, balanced, and secure energy system. Photoncycle systems enable households to use homegrown energy year-round for electricity, heat, and hot water, while also helping the grid balance production and consumption peaks. This enables the transition away from fossil-based energy.

Our customers are central to that mission. Every home we power is proof that energy independence is possible, and the stories of those homeowners are one of our strongest tools for reaching the next ones.

We are a team of 25 employees across offices in Oslo and Copenhagen. In 2026, we raised a €15 million Series A backed by NordicNinja, Voima Ventures, Lifeline Ventures, Eviny Ventures, Luminar Ventures and Momentum. We're now moving from full-scale pilot to commercial rollout, with the first phase of our production facility coming online in 2027.

The Role

We are looking for a Storyteller to own content creation and community management for our customers. Your main goal is to engage our customers with compelling, on-brand content, and to make Photoncycle something people want to follow, talk about and belong to.

You will shape how Photoncycle shows up on all communications channels, in both Danish and English. You will most likely start in a wind turbine development project that is still in its early stages. Working closely with experienced colleagues, you will review simulation results, apply engineering judgement to identify the next steps, and coordinate with teams across Turbine Loads, Software, Certification, Testing, and component design.

As you gain experience and the project progresses, you will also work with prototype data and support turbine validation activities at our test site in Østerild.

This is a hands-on engineering role focused on wind turbine controller development, tuning and validation. It is not a project management or software development position, although you will collaborate closely with both disciplines.

As a global product consultant, you will sit at the heart of Talent, bringing together L&D, Technology and regional stakeholders to transform how learning is curated, delivered and experienced across the firm.

**

• Partner with the Global L&D Product Owner and functional leads to set direction, align priorities and advance Microsoft Viva Learning as a global learning platform

• Drive adoption, engagement and measurable business impact across a complex global stakeholder landscape

**

• Strong background in Talent, Learning & Development or HR transformation

• Ability to influence senior stakeholders, navigate ambiguity and lead change in a complex global environment

This is a standout opportunity to help build a skills-led, experience-driven Talent ecosystem, powered by Microsoft Viva Learning — at global scale.

If you’re passionate about learning, product thinking and digital employee experience, we’d love to hear from you.

What we offer you

Are you ready to shape your future with confidence? Apply today.

To help create an equitable and inclusive experience during the recruitment process, please inform us as soon as possible about any disability-related adjustments or accommodations you may need.

**EY | Building a better working world

Enabled by data, AI and advanced technology, EY teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow.

Do you want to help build one coherent way for a global technology organization to deliver, bringing scaled product-centric ways of working project and program execution _together into a single system, rather than running them as separate worlds? Are you as comfortable helping shape that system and turning it into ways of working people actually use in the room with the people who'll actually use it?_We are hiring a Manager, Delivery Enablement to help shape and evolve how Pandora's D&T organization delivers. D&T spans the full range of technology that keeps Pandora running: from customer-facing platforms to manufacturing systems, ERP, logistics and operations, security, covering build, run, and operate across all of it. This role does not carry people-management responsibility. Your impact comes through the quality of what you build and how well it lands across the organization.

You'll join Delivery Enablement, a team combining operating-model design and implementation, coaching, and delivery tooling capability. It's built to make Digital & Technology (D&T) faster, clearer, and more coherent at scale. Delivery Enablement sits within Delivery Excellence, alongside the Scrum Masters, Delivery Leads, and Project and Program Managers. You will work with the wider team to shape ideas and turn them into practical ways of working across D&T.

**Your Role

**You will help harmonize and evolve how scaled agile delivery and more structured, plan-driven delivery work together, building on what already exists across D&T rather than replacing it, closing gaps only where they cause real friction. This is as much about leading change as it is about designing structure. You will also advise on structuring new or reshaping delivery entities (product lines, programs, organizational changes, or other setups) as they take shape, and help teams and entities build the capability to adopt the model as it evolves.

You will work closely with the wider delivery community, as well as product, engineering, and leadership more broadly, to facilitate structural workshops, build the case for change, and make sure what gets designed is something people actually want to use, not just a document on a shelf. A key part of the role is building the relationships, networks and momentum needed to bring ideas to life across D&T.

**Your Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Co-design and evolve how scaled agile and structured, plan-driven delivery work together, harmonizing and building on existing practice rather than replacing it

• Advise on structuring new or reshaping delivery entities (product lines, programs, organizational changes, or other setups) as they take shape

• Lead workstreams that take new or improved delivery processes (for example dependency management or capacity planning) from idea through pilot, rollout, adoption and continuous improvement

• Support onboarding and capability-building for teams and entities adopting the model, working alongside the team's wider coaching capability

• Facilitate structural workshops and working sessions with the wider delivery community to shape and pressure-test the model

• Build relationships, networks and communities that help change spread and stick across D&T

• Pilot approaches, learn from feedback, and scale what works

• Help translate high-level decisions about how delivery is prioritized, funded, resourced, and executed into practical structures and standards teams can use

• Help projects and programs connect into the wider D&T Operating Model, including common governance, planning, dependency management and delivery tooling

• Contribute to keeping the model coherent as it evolves, spotting where new structures overlap or conflict with what already exists

• Provide point-in-time advisory support where operating-model gaps are most costly

• Document how the operating model works and how it evolves over time

• Build strong relationships across the wider delivery community and leadership to ensure what gets built is genuinely adopted

**What Is Needed To Succeed

**

• ignificant experience in delivery transformation, operating-model implementation, PMO, program/project delivery or organizational change within a large, complex technology organization

• Demonstrated experience working across both scaled/product-centric agile delivery and more structured, plan-driven delivery, with enough understanding to contribute credibly to how they work together

• Track record of taking new ways of working from idea through implementation, adoption and continuous improvement

• Ideally a mix of hands-on delivery experience and consulting or advisory experience, but real, first-hand delivery experience matters more than advisory polish alone

• Strong stakeholder management, facilitation, and narrative-building skills across senior and operational levels

• Comfortable leading through organizational change: helping people, not just structures, adapt as delivery models shift

• Able to build trust, networks and momentum without relying on formal authority

• Comfortable using AI tools to accelerate your own analysis, design, and documentation work

• Working understanding of how delivery tooling (e.g. Jira/Confluence, or equivalent) underpins an operating model, enough to design frameworks that translate into practice, not to configure the tooling yourself

• Comfortable operating in ambiguity: building on foundations already in motion, while still shaping significant parts of the model from scratch

• Systems thinking: able to see cross-domain and cross-entity dependencies, not just local fixes

• Pragmatic bias toward incremental, adoptable change over comprehensive upfront design

• Relevant certifications (e.g. PMP, PRINCE2, SAFe) are an advantage

If you see yourself in the role and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply! We are an international team, so please make sure to send us your application in English to be considered. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

**Icing on the cake

**You will be working out of our beautiful Digital & Technology Hub in Copenhagen, in a rapidly growing environment of highly skilled and experienced colleagues, which is a key initiative that goes along with Pandora’s experience & ambitions.Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

About Envira

Envira turns satellite and geospatial data into climate-risk intelligence for banks, insurers and public authorities. Envira Flood covers flood and storm-surge risk at building level; Envira Agro covers crop and climate risk across agricultural portfolios. We're based in Copenhagen and won the EU Big Data from Space Award 2025 plus the Danish Grunddataprisen 2026.

The role

Full-time, on-site in Copenhagen five days a week. You'll own the platforms our customers use, working closely with our data scientists and leadership, with real influence on how our products are built and run. This isn't a standard corporate job: we're looking for people who ship and want to grow fast. There will be pressure, and real ownership to match.

What you'll work on

• Building and extending our web platforms and APIs

• Connecting our geospatial data and risk models to customer-facing applications

• Running and improving our Azure infrastructure: deployment, monitoring and reliability

• Data security and access control, in line with what financial-sector customers expect

Our stack

Python and FastAPI · React and TypeScript · Postgres · Azure · Docker

About you

• Newly graduated or up to 3–4 years of experience, with a degree in computer science, engineering or similar

• You've built something, run it in production yourself, and kept it running

• Comfortable across backend, infrastructure and frontend

• You use AI tools daily, and review, question and discard what they produce when it's wrong

• You prefer small, simple solutions that work over impressive architecture

• You raise problems early and make decisions without waiting to be told

• You live in Denmark and can work from our Copenhagen office five days a week. We don't offer remote work or visa sponsorship

Our working language is English; Danish is a plus.

What we offer

• Salary based on experience, with potential for warrants

• Free lunch at the office

• Ownership of real products used by banks, insurers and public authorities

• The opportunity for tremendous growth

Our process

Short screening call → two-hour practical task on realistic data with your usual AI tools (no whiteboard puzzles) → interview where you walk us through your solution and meet the team.

How to apply

Please apply through our application form (about 10 minutes; we ask for your CV, grades, GitHub link and salary expectation). We review applications on a rolling basis, so apply early.

PanTarg is a Danish biotechnology company developing novel anti-cancer therapies in the form of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) for the treatment of aggressive cancers with high unmet medical need.

Our work is based on more than 30 years of research conducted at Rigshospitalet and University of Copenhagen, and our vision is to enable novel treatment options for cancer patients via a novel first-in-class approach to targeted therapy.

We are currently incubated at the BioInnovation Institute (BII), a Copenhagen-based incubation hub for biotech startups in Europe. Here, we are currently progressing through preclinical development, aiming to reach a stage of clinical testing within a few years.

The position

We are looking for a scientist to join our team on site at BII. We are primarily looking for a candidate with several years of hands-on experience, especially within immunohistochemistry (IHC) techniques and target expression analyses. The candidate will be responsible for generating and analyzing data that will be essential for several key readouts and business decisions, including safety assessments and clinical indication selection.

Qualifications

• 
Primary qualification: Documented experience in histology and IHC, including target/biomarker scoring, tissue microarrays (TMA), and spatial analysis. Experience with tissue handling, sectioning, and staining is highly desirable, ideally combined with experience using digital image-analysis software such as QuPath or equivalent.

• 
The optimal candidate will have obtained a PhD degree and have at least 3-5 years of experience from either pharma, biotech, or as a post doc. Robust and documented (5+ years) relevant hands-on experience without a PhD degree may also be acceptable, if the primary qualification is met.

• 
Secondary qualification: Hands-on experience with in vitro biology & pharmacology in the form of mammalian cell culture, in vitro dose-response studies and characterization of drug activity, cell viability/cytotoxicity assays, flow cytometry, ELISA, and related cellular assays, will be a highly desired skillset.

• 
Good scientific communications skills, and the ability to clearly and precisely present data to a professional audience.

• 
Good interpersonal skills, and the ability to thrive in a startup environment where flexibility and a can-do attitude is part of everyday work life.

• 
Fluent in the English language, written as well as spoken.

General information and how to apply

• 
You will be reporting to the Chief Scientific Officer.

• 
The position is full time, and on-site presence at the BioInnovation Institute in Copenhagen will be required.

• 
Interviews will be conducted on an ongoing basis, and the selected candidate will start as soon as possible.

• 
Application takes place via the application system here at LinkedIn.

• 
Please provide and combine, in a single file for the LinkedIn application system, a one-page CV, as well as a short, motivated application letter (also one page), summarizing your relevant experience, key responsibilities in previous roles, and motivation for applying for the position.

At Factbird, we help manufacturers see what’s really happening on their lines, so they can make better, faster decisions. Our plug-and-play hardware and cloud platform turn live production data into clear insights, and we’re scaling fast across sites, teams, and countries.

We’re looking for a hands-on Senior IoT Solutions Engineer to join Engineering Services, the team that takes on the technical problems that fall outside what our product and Support handle today. You’ll look at a PLC, a sensor, or a 20-year-old CNC and work out how to get its data into Factbird. Sales and Support turn to you when the answer is “it depends,” and you turn that into a clear yes, no, or “here’s how.” Then you write it down so the next person doesn’t need to ask.

About the role

Engineering Services solves the hardest technical problems, documents them, and shares the knowledge, so Factbird gets smarter and the same problem doesn’t come back. You’ll answer feasibility questions before deals close, design and build custom solutions, and fix the cross-domain problems no other team can place.

**

The team mission we are on:** Engineering Services is a small team of experts finding solutions to a wide variety of challenges. In pre-sales we are supporting our AE's and Solution Consultants with feasibility testing the most complex customer setups or requirements. Often directly with the customers and their technical teams. In post-sales we collaborate with Cloud, FW and HW teams, and build and support a range of custom solutions. Our core mission is to increase documentation, standardization and empowering our colleagues in both pre- and post-sales roles to server the customers in the most technical cases.

What You'll Do

• Answer feasibility questions from Sales: can we connect this machine, PLC, or sensor, and how

• Design and build custom solutions: logic boxes, signal converters, IO-Link modules, EDGE flows, and Factbird® powered by OMRON NX1 programs that fill gaps the cloud platform can’t handle yet.

• Design the integration: map the customer’s OT/IT environment and plan the data sources, tag structures, transformations, and security.

• Root cause troubleshooting in live production. Smaller share of time, highest stakes

• Document everything you build and fix: Solution Records, runbooks, and wiring guides for customers and internal teams, clear enough that someone else can pick it up. Version and back up every configuration.

• Bench-test hardware before it ships, test the full data flow end to end (including failure recovery and restarts), and hand hardware to Logistics with a clear packing list.

• Integrate customer systems through Kepware, Ignition, OPC UA, MQTT, EtherNet/IP, Modbus, and Node-RED.

• Share what you know: help Support, Solution Consultants, and Hardware handle more on their own.

• Streamline as you go: spot repeat work and clunky processes, and fix them or flag them. Build templates and scripts that make the next delivery faster.

• Turn repeat workarounds into product input with a business case, so the workaround can disappear.

• Join customer and prospect calls as the technical voice alongside Solution Consultants and Account Managers.

About you

You’re an experienced industrial automation engineer, as happy with a screwdriver as with a terminal. You know how factories work, and you’re comfortable saying “not directly, but here’s the route.”

You document like the next person depends on it, because they do. You can’t leave a clunky process alone: you always have an eye on how to make things simpler and more repeatable.

You’re flexible and self-directed: you take a high level of accountability and ownership. You can prioritize and deliver without daily supervision, and you troubleshoot systematically when things get ambiguous. The work changes week to week, and the team’s shape will keep evolving as Factbird grows. You’re happy to do what’s needed today while helping move things in a more scalable direction.

You love being the expert, but you equally love teaching others and making the teams around you smarter. And most of all, you care about making the answer simple for whoever asked.

Requirements:

• A bachelor's degree in automation, electrical engineering, mechatronics, or similar, or equivalent hands-on experience.

• At least 5 years in industrial automation or controls engineering, including hands-on work on the shop floor (7+ years preferred).

• Hands-on PLC experience with at least one major vendor, e.g. Siemens, Omron, or Rockwell/Allen-Bradley.

• Solid understanding of industrial protocols, e.g. OPC UA, Modbus, EtherNet/IP, MQTT.

• Working knowledge of sensors and signals, like digital, analog (4–20 mA, 0–10 V), IO-Link, PNP/NPN, and energy metering.

• Root cause analysis across hardware, networks, and software in live production environments.

• Field experience commissioning or troubleshooting equipment in live plants.

• Comfortable troubleshooting site networks, e.g. IP setup, routers, SIMs, and firewalls.

• A clear communicator in English who can explain technical trade-offs to non-engineers.

• A strong documentation habit: when you build it, you write it down.

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn’t one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Company-wide kickoffs & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what’s next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We’re proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

**We’d love to hear from you

**If this role feels like a match, we’d be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.
